clue.text: Wolves player who roams around aimlessly?

blocks.note: Wolves is the nickname of an English football club from Wolverhampton; the answer is its full name's second word, singular

explanation.surface: A footballer who drifts about the pitch with no idea of his position.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club, so any of its players is a Wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wolves player plays for the Wanderers, and a wanderer is literally someone who roams aimlessly.

clue.text: Long nail finally broke

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a pin is a small nail

explanation.surface: A long fingernail has just snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Long is the verb here, as in to long for something, not the adjective the surface pairs with nail.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to yearn for something absent, as a homesick exile does.

clue.text: Person from institution’s given home with couple

explanation.surface: Someone released from an institution is sent home along with a pair of companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Couple is a verb here: animals that couple mate.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is someone held in a prison or asylum.

clue.text: Church programme includes top lay musician

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its first letter

blocks.note: a list of items, as a programme is

explanation.surface: A church's order of service features a leading lay musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Lay here means not ordained, one of the congregation rather than clergy; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist is a musician who plays the cello.

clue.text: Designer has last of mini skirts in Twiggy’s size

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so the last of mini is its closing I
the edges of a word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: Mary Quant, the designer who popularised the miniskirt

explanation.surface: Mary Quant's miniskirts come in the size the 1960s model Twiggy wore.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was the 1960s London fashion designer behind the miniskirt, and Twiggy was the model of the same era; skirts looks like clothing but is the verb for edging a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Size and quantity both mean amount or magnitude.

clue.text: Essentially policed crime surrounding alcohol shop

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its middle

explanation.surface: A crime near a liquor store gets only token attention from the police.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-licence is the British name for a shop selling alcohol to take away, like a liquor store.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-licence is licensed to sell alcohol for drinking off the premises.

clue.text: Stalls in Kitzbuhel initially keeping old among new skis

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the word's opening letter is used
the letters of skis are made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Stalls in an Austrian ski resort stock old gear among the new skis.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitzbuhel is an Austrian ski resort; the O goes after the I of the rearranged skis.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiosks are small stalls selling newspapers, snacks and the like.

clue.text: Artist, leader of innovation in movement and light

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, here the I of innovation
in places one thing inside another

explanation.surface: An artist who pioneered new work in dance and lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the glow given off by the sun or a lamp, and the surface hides it by making light sound like stage lighting.

clue.text: Aunt losing housing, just not right

indicators.note: the outside of AUNT, its first and last letters, is dropped

blocks.note: AUNT without its outer A and T

explanation.surface: An aunt is evicted and it seems simply wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Just wants to be read as merely; here it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Right here is the moral sense, just or proper, and its negation is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Unemployed setter had clues every now and then

indicators.note: something done every now and then happens at intervals, so the letters are taken at regular gaps: second, fourth

blocks.note: the setter is I, so the setter had = I'd

explanation.surface: An out-of-work crossword setter only produced clues occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the writer of the puzzle, so it stands for I; I had shortens to I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means out of work, not employed.

clue.text: Finally corrected all tags on toys with 75% off

indicators.note: the letters are put right, rearranged
three of the four letters of toys go, leaving the first

blocks.note: TOYS losing three quarters of its letters

explanation.surface: A shop has at last fixed the price tags on its toys, which are now 75% off.
explanation.walkthrough: Finally looks like it tells you to take a last letter, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom matching the adverb: said with relief when something long awaited finally happens.

clue.text: Look online for live coverage of disputes

explanation.surface: Searching the internet for live news reports of disputes.
explanation.walkthrough: Live coverage suggests a broadcast; here BE covers ROWS. Rows, rhyming with cows, is British for arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: The computing sense of an older word for grazing or leafing through books, now used for surfing the web.

clue.text: Big draw in twitching day’s curlew, maybe

indicators.note: twitching means jerking restlessly, so the letters cannot keep still in their order

blocks.note: D = day, the abbreviation used in dates and diaries

explanation.surface: A curlew was the big attraction on a birdwatching day.
explanation.walkthrough: Twitching is British slang for keen birdwatching, which makes the surface fit the answer; here it jumbles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The curlew is a long-billed bird that wades in mud, one example of a wading bird.

clue.text: Lawyer’s bag?

blocks.note: the surface suggests a briefcase; a lawyer's actual business is a suit or a case in court
the question mark lets bag be an ordinary piece of luggage

explanation.surface: A briefcase belonging to a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: Suit and case both mean a lawsuit, so a lawyer's business is a suit-case; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The luggage is literally a bag, and the pun splits it into two legal words for a lawsuit.

clue.text: Even with exam mark reduced by university, a first in Linguistics

indicators.note: GRADE loses its last letter
the first in a word is its opening letter, borrowing the university grade the surface is about

explanation.surface: A student still got a first in Linguistics despite a marked-down exam.
explanation.walkthrough: A first is a top British degree grade, which the surface uses; the clue wants the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradual slope or rise is an even one, without sudden steps.

clue.text: Working in Canada, startled to see huge snake

indicators.note: the letters of Canada jump about

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone working in Canada is shocked to come across an enormous snake.
explanation.walkthrough: There are no anacondas in Canada, which is the joke of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a very large South American snake.

clue.text: Decay in waste producing toxin

indicators.note: the letters are laid waste, broken up

explanation.surface: Rotting rubbish gives off a poison.
explanation.walkthrough: Waste reads as rubbish in the surface; here it is a verb, to wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the classic fast-acting poison of detective fiction.

clue.text: Detective’s men reportedly under cover

explanation.surface: A detective's officers are working undercover.
explanation.walkthrough: Under cover suggests one phrase; under places the men below the detective, and cover alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A disguise covers who you really are.

clue.text: Fence in space nearby

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Put a fence up in the space next door.
explanation.walkthrough: In belongs to the definition, not to a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the phrasal verb: surrounding a field with a barrier so nothing gets out.

clue.text: Insist head coach’s right leaving

indicators.note: right leaving means the R departs from the word, so TRAIN drops it

explanation.surface: Insisting that the head coach should be allowed to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach is the verb to train, not a sports manager.
explanation.definitionFit: The sense of asserting firmly, as when someone maintains their innocence, rather than keeping something in repair.

clue.text: Online image for travel centre’s American sailor

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, and with six letters that is the two in the middle

explanation.surface: A travel hub's website shows a picture of a US sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: A tar, or jack tar, is an old word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A computing sense of a Hindu word for a god's earthly form: the picture standing in for you on a website.

clue.text: Special care, ewes we lost returning to fold

indicators.note: the letters of care are made special, rearranged
ewes that have lost we no longer have those two letters, leaving ES
the remaining ES goes back to front

blocks.note: EWES minus WE is ES, turned round

explanation.surface: Special care is needed as some ewes went missing coming back to the sheepfold.
explanation.walkthrough: Fold looks like a sheep pen, fitting the ewes; it is the crease in paper or cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold here is the line pressed into paper or cloth, not the sheep pen the ewes suggest; the noun sense is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Scout out money for business

indicators.note: the letters are out of place

explanation.surface: Scouting around for cash to fund a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Scout out reads as one phrasal verb; out is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom is the trade a shop gets from its customers, its business.

clue.text: Graduate doctor weeps, admitting student cheats

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, as a door admits a visitor

explanation.surface: A newly qualified doctor breaks down on learning a student cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheats is the verb here, not a noun for dishonest people.
explanation.definitionFit: To bamboozle someone is to trick or cheat them.

clue.text: College vote retains sport as essential principle

blocks.note: a cross on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A college ballot keeps sport at the heart of its values.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union is a popular British sport, abbreviated RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for cross, now used for the heart of a problem or argument; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Pass time with young horse

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Spending time with a young horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Pass time reads as one idea, killing time; pass is the mountain gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, loosely: strictly it is a male under four, and the clue's broader phrase covers it.

clue.text: Shook container with wine

explanation.surface: Someone shook a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Container looks like a container instruction; it is simply a JAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense, of a sudden jolt that rattles something or someone.

clue.text: See fewer without sin

explanation.surface: Seeing fewer people once you give up sinning.
explanation.walkthrough: See wants to be a church see or a noun; here it is the verb, to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotless character is morally unblemished, without sin.
